integrity: 7 distinct company-paid jobs, no prior numbered case recycled; seller offers are M2, named vendor clients are not buyer proof, buyer Reddit self report M3 without invoice

cases.payer: UK/Irish Shopify retailer with regular product launches
cases.trigger: New SKU data and variant changes must be published accurately without distracting staff
cases.money_evidence: Named outsourcing firm advertises $4/hr or $680/month full-time; external e-commerce operator advertises 10–100 hours/month at $10–15/hr as recruitment offer, not payment
cases.complete_paid_outcome: From supplier records/photos to working published Shopify products, variants, metafields and corrected images
cases.convenience_vs_nonsoftware: Money buys human cleansing, uncertain supplier detail, catalogue editorial and marketplace fixes; pure CSV import a small fraction
cases.input_output: Supplier item lists + authorized Shopify shop -> live listings with matching SKU/variant and exceptions
cases.verification: Official CSV schema, bulk editor and Shopify live product readback; platform warns variant ID changes can destroy dependencies
cases.competitors: Shopify CSV/bulk editor; Matrixify-style bulk migration apps; $4/hr managed operator
cases.repeat_ai: General AI can prepare CSV from clean supplier tables and validate schema, cannot reliably infer missing facts or handle store-specific variants unattended
cases.ai_build: Creating a Shopify product uploader is straightforward; hard work is input truth and avoiding destructive updates, with many cheap alternatives
cases.recurrence_first_ten: Recurring uploads possible; first ten could be UK shop owners who publicly recruit VAs, but no ten confirmed matched buyers or app-selection reason
cases.strongest_kill: Native import and very cheap fully managed labour already cover bounded output; what remains is business owner approvals/content knowledge
cases.cheapest_falsification: Find a paid repeat owner who needs source-to-live autonomous updates with stable and complete source records, outside native CSV/bulk tools

cases.payer: Independent UK clothing label commissioning a factory tech-pack
cases.trigger: New garment range must be manufacturing-specified before factory sample quote
cases.money_evidence: UK marketplace lists detailed tech-pack buyer job with 54 freelance proposals and mean bid about £112; bidder rates are not buyer payment; freelance provider says from £40/hour for fit and tech packs
cases.complete_paid_outcome: Manufacturer-ready apparel specification with construction, fabric, trims, graded measures, and tolerances
cases.convenience_vs_nonsoftware: Supplier and maker are primarily paid for apparel construction knowhow, fitting and fabric behaviour, rather than document arrangement
cases.input_output: Founder sketch and measurements -> technically complete construction tech pack factory can quote and sample from
cases.verification: Factory can review field completeness; real fit, garment construction and tolerances need experienced pattern cutter and physical samples
cases.competitors: UK tech-pack freelance specialists; Techpacker and CLO3D design systems
cases.repeat_ai: AI can populate a template but invents hidden seam/construction decisions and tolerances; repeat accepted factory output unproven
cases.ai_build: Template generator simple; sample/fit feedback and spec exception handling remain human service
cases.recurrence_first_ten: Fashion founder directories and posted briefs, but no ten spending repeatingly on *automatable* pack subset
cases.strongest_kill: A £112 bid is NOT £112 spend; full job is expert apparel engineering and factory communication
cases.cheapest_falsification: Do not revive without a defined, documented factory validator for a pre-approved tech pack variant

cases.payer: UK brand/agency buying constant packaging changes
cases.trigger: Seasonal or variant packaging artwork needs frequent revisions without hiring a designer
cases.money_evidence: Current Manchester service advertises dedicated designer £699–£1,099/month; named customer testimonials on vendor site, not independent payment verification
cases.complete_paid_outcome: Complete brand-approved packaging designs, dieline-ready files and repeat revisions on request
cases.convenience_vs_nonsoftware: Monthly fee buys reserved UK designer capacity and taste + collaboration, not only file export
cases.input_output: Brand system + packaging dimensions/product copy -> accepted branded artwork for printer
cases.verification: Preflight bleeds/text checks are mechanisable; visual acceptance and legal ingredients need human review
cases.competitors: Design Cloud, Kimp, Adobe Illustrator and Canva teams; exact paid incumbent itself
cases.repeat_ai: AI repeats visual variants quickly; commercial brand fidelity, typography and proofs still require accountable art director
cases.ai_build: AI-built editor competes with incumbent design platforms, not £699/mo named designer, and active request queue is real service
cases.recurrence_first_ten: Ongoing repeat work, but no demonstrable independent £699/mo fully automatable layer or ten buyers
cases.strongest_kill: Actual fee attaches to designer as capacity; narrow print-ready pass already killed in previous batch
cases.cheapest_falsification: Independently verify repeated pay for deterministic SKU variant adaptation with brand-approved source templates, no human art direction

cases.payer: Independent UK estate agency publishing new property listings weekly
cases.trigger: Seller photo batch needs overnight white-label retouch + correct branding
cases.money_evidence: UK external listing studio publicly offers £0.40–£1.40/image, monthly volume discounts; no proven buyer receipts
cases.complete_paid_outcome: Edited listing-quality exposures, balanced windows, sky replacements and branded delivered photo sets
cases.convenience_vs_nonsoftware: Core convenience is overnight staff labour, photo discretion and fast reliable batch handling; product only auto-filters
cases.input_output: Raw agency photos + style guide -> Rightmove/Zoopla-ready set in correct order/format
cases.verification: Pixel resolution, count and agency specifications testable; window/housing authenticity and aesthetic approval subjective
cases.competitors: Aftershoot and Lightroom batch presets; outsourced full editing providers at similar very low prices
cases.repeat_ai: AI image batch tools already accomplish standard exposure/sky corrections; difficult glass/reflection artifacts need retouch
cases.ai_build: New batch processor possible but highly commoditised, with existing dedicated estate photo tools
cases.recurrence_first_ten: Per-listing recurring potential, but 100 images yields just £40 at floor rate; ten named purchase-ready agencies not evidenced
cases.strongest_kill: Low unit price and readily automated edits; ongoing volume needs acquisition and human art correction to earn service fee
cases.cheapest_falsification: Find external agency independently paying >£500/mo for *digital-only*, repeatably verifiable editing despite AI tools; otherwise do not revive

cases.payer: UK large-range Amazon reseller with frequent suppressed ASINs
cases.trigger: Monthly catalogue suppression and variation errors jeopardise live sales
cases.money_evidence: Managed reseller-side Amazon catalogue provider advertises £960/month for around 200 SKUs and names clients A Kilo of Spices and Aroma Concepts; testimonials vendor-hosted
cases.complete_paid_outcome: Amazon ASINs restored to buyable/searchable live status and maintained, not just error alerts
cases.convenience_vs_nonsoftware: The spend buys Seller Support escalations, commercial assortment decisions, restricted claims decisions and operator ownership as well as repeat fixes
cases.input_output: Authorized Seller Central listings + official attribute errors -> compliant submitted records with buyability/status receipt
cases.verification: Amazon SP-API returns synchronous/asynchronous listing issues and status notifications; no guarantee policy appeals and category discretion automated
cases.competitors: Amazon SP-API native notifications, Kangaroo paid operators, Amazon tools and category specialists
cases.repeat_ai: AI can suggest required attribute corrections from schemas, not guarantee accepted live ASIN where Amazon policy judgment intervenes
cases.ai_build: AI-built software can automate schema-compliant submissions and read status, but principal platform has oracle and operator escalation remains
cases.recurrence_first_ten: 200+ SKU UK resellers reachable via Amazon brands, ten verified with same suppressions and buying intent unproven
cases.strongest_kill: Full purchased restoration includes case management/manual access; stripping these out recreates cheap feature, not £960/month job
cases.cheapest_falsification: Buyer reports recurring suppressed ASIN cause that is resolvable through documented API alone, independent of Seller Support

cases.payer: UK manufacturer/translation agency needing international print brochures
cases.trigger: Approved translations must be placed back into editable multilingual brochure artwork
cases.money_evidence: Specialist UK DTP provider lists £45 minimum for seven pages, then £6/page European and £8/page non-European-language layout
cases.complete_paid_outcome: Print-ready, correctly typeset localized art retaining line breaks and all approved translated content
cases.convenience_vs_nonsoftware: Digitally delivered output is separable from actual translation; higher-end spend covers typographic judgement in text expansion/RTL and printer QA
cases.input_output: Approved original InDesign/Illustrator files plus translated text -> updated print-ready language editions
cases.verification: Fonts, overset, bleed, language glyph support can be checked via Adobe tools; visual reading order and contextual art must be manually validated
cases.competitors: InDesign scripting/IDML, Adobe translation localization partners and low per-page dedicated DTP provider
cases.repeat_ai: LLM can suggest line shortening and automated layout, but can corrupt translated approved text or RTL visually
cases.ai_build: A DTP automation engine feasible but incumbent tooling scripts and £6/page human QA leave no significant entry margin
cases.recurrence_first_ten: Recurring multi-language production possible, no independent identified UK buyer paid use for standalone program or ten prospect list
cases.strongest_kill: €500/mo thesis weak at £6/page given custom source formats and QA, while same supplier can provide full output
cases.cheapest_falsification: Only if 10+ manufacturers show high-volume repeat approved source templates and willing third-party self-service usage

cases.payer: Small-business owner with WordPress website who cannot handle updates
cases.trigger: Ongoing hosting, content edits and basic maintenance outsourced monthly
cases.money_evidence: Public r/smallbusiness account says currently paying 130 monthly including tax for host, maintain and content updates; currency not specified in post and cannot assume GBP
cases.complete_paid_outcome: Website stays online and secure with small content changes completed on request
cases.convenience_vs_nonsoftware: Buyer-side self-report of separate agency payment despite software CMS; the fee includes human availability/support and hosting
cases.input_output: Website admin credentials + small edit request -> published change and operation/restore if required

cases.competitors: WordPress built-in visual editor, Wix/Squarespace managed offerings and low-cost UK web care plans
cases.repeat_ai: AI agents can accomplish simple page edits given permission but fail to assume hosting incident response securely without human supervision
cases.ai_build: AI-built website bot introduces credential/security burden and still needs ongoing on-call support
cases.recurrence_first_ten: Other UK SMEs plausibly reachable through trade associations but ten specifically paying for external edits and seeking replacement not identified
cases.strongest_kill: Actual monthly fee is for trustworthy whole-site stewardship rather than only typing blog posts; small price cannot pay acquisition plus emergencies
cases.cheapest_falsification: Find buyer who independently pays only for objective fixed-scope site edit batches, excluding hosting and incident response
